text:
maria: FYI we had messy handoffs in yesterday's partner SEV with CloudForge. partner couldn't tell who to reach for the bridge so they started paging multiple ppl.
omar: saw the thread. root cause = liaison rotation wasn't posted to the shared channel and partner DMed a couple engineers.
jess: let's make one clear public policy in the shared channel: primary liaison = current oncall, secondary = partnership lead. short and visible.
liam: agree. also pin a tiny checklist: bridge URL, phone escalation list, current liaison, escalation order, quick mapping of which Redwood team to call for infra vs runtime.
sophia: i'll draft that pinned blurb + a one-paragraph "what happens during an incident" flow. @akshay can you review the wording from a support tolerance perspective?
akshay: yep. quick thought: do we page partners directly on the first alert or page our oncall and then invite the partner? i prefer the latter to avoid noisy partner pages.
omar: same. recommended flow: page -> oncall ack within 15m -> triage -> create shared bridge -> invite partner liaison if needed.
partner-bot: [automated] Template available: /templates/marketplace-sev-bridge. Use `/partner-sev start --template marketplace-sev-bridge` to open a shared bridge with partner channel autofill.
jess: nice. sophia, include that slash command snippet and a short example in the pinned message. also add: if bridge creation fails, fallback to phone tree; last-resort: create a temporary shared channel and escalate.
maria: for rotations: propose we publish liaison coverage weekly with a single-line handoff at the start of the coverage window (ex: "liaison: liam — Mon 00:00 to Sun 23:59 UTC").
liam: i'll take weekly coverage for the next 8 weeks to stabilize this pattern and document schedule in partnership-runbooks.
akshay: put partner-facing SLOs in the pin: ack 15m, triage 30m, bridge up <1h. also auto-escalate to partnership manager oncall after two missed ack windows.
sophia: will mark those as "partner-facing response targets" so expectations are explicit.
omar: add a small mapping table: GPU/serving runtime -> #eng-runtime, network/storage -> #eng-infra, SI integration -> #partner-ops. that'll speed routing.
jess: also require any partner that wants direct paging to sign a brief escalation agreement (and run a test drill) so we can validate channels and contact numbers.
maria: agreed. action items recap: sophia drafts pin + SLOs, akshay reviews, jess adds slash snippet, liam publishes schedule in runbooks, omar sets recurring monthly sync with partner ops to review contacts. i'll link the runbook PR back here when it's opened.
partner-bot: [automated] Reminder scheduled: partner-contact-sync (monthly) -> next run 2024-04-03 15:00 UTC.
liam: small addendum — include a short note on which escalation path to use for a hardware failure vs model-serving failure. saves time.
akshay: +1. add a two-line triage decision: hardware (board/fan/power) -> eng-infra, model perf/KV cache -> eng-runtime, integration break -> partner-ops.
sophia: drafting now. will add phone tree + a Zapier fallback note (low-confidence) in case bridge tooling is down.
jess: can we run a 20-min tabletop with CloudForge ops this month to exercise the flow? helps uncover gaps.
omar: i'll coordinate dates with the partner PM.
maria: thanks everyone. sophia please post the draft by EOD Friday. akshay please approve or comment within 48h. once approved, liam will publish weekly liaison schedule and pin the message in the shared channel.
akshay: noted.
(akshay left the channel) :thumbsup:
